evidence: The milestone snapshot's src/styles.css has 1,380 lines; the file is entirely new in this diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the plans and help selectors (including their media-query overrides) into page-level CSS files, import them from their owning page components, and keep only shared rules in styles.css; verify the four views at desktop and mobile widths for cascade changes.
findings.title: Split the stylesheet that crosses 1,000 lines
findings.why_it_matters: The new global stylesheet is 1,380 lines and now contains separate workbench, plans, help, modal, and responsive sections. A change to one page's styles must be traced through the shared base rules and a long responsive block, making cascade interactions across pages harder to review. Move the plans and help rules with their responsive overrides into page-level stylesheets, following the existing history.css pattern, and leave shared primitives in styles.css.

validation.reason: The new 1,380-line global stylesheet mixes plans and help selectors with workbench rules and places their responsive overrides in shared media blocks, so extracting those page-specific rules would make future page edits and cascade review materially more local, as the existing history.css arrangement demonstrates.

findings.suggested_fix: After await f.text(), merge incoming plans against the latest plans state, preferably through a ref kept current by every successful persist or a single serialized mutation path; then write the merged state. Add a deferred File.text test that deletes or saves a plan before import resolves.
findings.title: Pending plan import can undo newer plan changes
findings.why_it_matters: A user can start importing a JSON file and then delete a plan while the file is being read. When the read completes, the import uses the plans array captured before deletion and persists it, bringing the deleted plan back. A save made during the read can likewise disappear. Build the merged list from the latest plans state when the file read completes, and serialize the read and write against other plan mutations.

validation.reason: The plan import callback resumes after await f.text() with its pre-read plans closure, while deletion and saving remain available and persist newer state, so its later persist([...fresh, ...plans]) can restore a deleted plan or discard a newer save.

findings.suggested_fix: Track a monotonically increasing selection ID in a ref. Increment it when starting an import and when restoring demo; after await f.text(), only set all/source/notice/error if the ID still matches. Cover out-of-order file reads and restore during a pending import.
findings.title: History import can overwrite a newer data choice
findings.why_it_matters: A user can choose a CSV, then click Restore demo or choose another CSV while the first file is still being read. The earlier import may finish last and replace the newer dataset, so the page shows data contrary to the latest selection. Give each import and restore action a generation number and ignore completions from earlier generations.

validation.reason: History import awaits f.text() without a generation check, while Restore demo and another file selection can update all/source/notice during that wait, allowing the older read to finish last and overwrite the user's newer choice.
